subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server intermittently produces no model events for 120s, then profile cooldown causes cascading fallbacks

question: Should an OpenClaw-generated model-silent idle timeout affect only the current attempt, or temporarily cool down that same model for every concurrent lane using the auth profile?
rationale: Current main deliberately shares timeout state at model scope, but this report shows that one uncertain app-server attempt can suppress unrelated same-model work; the desired circuit-breaker tradeoff cannot be inferred safely from source alone.

options.title: Attempt-local idle timeout
options.body: Do not mutate shared profile health for a locally generated silent-attempt timeout unless Codex or a provider-health probe supplies model/profile failure evidence.

options.title: Keep shared model cooldown
options.body: Retain the existing same-model circuit breaker and limit the repair to diagnosing and reducing zero-event Codex turns.

options.title: Short silent-turn quarantine
options.body: Introduce a distinct, very short same-model quarantine for silent attempts while preserving normal cooldowns for upstream timeouts and rate limits.

recommendation.title: Attempt-local idle timeout
recommendation.body: Do not mutate shared profile health for a locally generated silent-attempt timeout unless Codex or a provider-health probe supplies model/profile failure evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the current progress-aware Codex watchdog and has the strongest historical connection across the runner and lane-timeout boundary.
